abstract: Cortical excitability, characterized by the rapid polymerization and de-polymerization of cortical F-actin, has been reported in a variety of systems and cell types. In X. laevis, C. elegans, and echinoderm embryos, these oscillations are dependent on the small GTPase, Rho, which is regulated in turn by F-actin dependent negative feedback. We sought to investigate whether the Rho family GTPases, Cdc42 and Rac, contribute to specific regulation of F-actin waves and what feedback drives these dynamics. Using an artificial cortex system consisting of Xenopus egg extract and supported lipid bilayers, we showed that active Cdc42 and active Rac are dynamically patterned in a manner that is coordinated with active Rho and F-actin, suggesting that they contribute to the previously defined oscillatory circuit. We found that total Cdc42 and Rac cortical activity depends on Rho activity. Conversely, Rho activity and F-actin wave dynamics are modulated by Cdc42 and Rac activity. We determined that Cdc42 and Rac are differentially regulated by known regulators of the oscillatory circuit, including Ect2 and F-actin polymerization. We also observed that Rho and Cdc42 are segregated into defined activity zones by microtubule plus-end overlaps, presenting a possible mechanism for the division plane-specific F-actin wave dynamics. Our findings demonstrate that the major Rho family members participate in the cortical excitability circuit and reveal additional mechanisms that regulate Rho and F-actin waves. Additionally, this work supports a model wherein spatial segregation of Rho family GTPases differentially modulates cortical pattern dynamics.
